result.summary:
Applied §11.9.4's single-statement reorder exactly as specified in test/support/tenant_template.ex's ensure_template!/0 -- compiles clean, formats clean -- then found a SECOND, DIFFERENT, PRE-EXISTING defect while running §11.7's required regression plan. This is not a recurrence of the Mechanism-4 bug §11.9 fixed; §11.9's own fix works exactly as designed. It is an unrelated, previously-undiscovered bug in provision_via_shared_connection/1's teardown wrapping (introduced in commit c38dfa9b, the SAME implementation step that first introduced provision_via_shared_connection/1 itself, per design §11.2/§11.3) that makes every async:false + template::clone TenantFixture caller's teardown intermittently -- in fact, in every run observed -- fail with a distinct symptom. Reported as a BLOCKER per this handoff's own instruction, not patched around, since fixing it means either changing test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (outside this handoff's §11.9.4 authorization, which scopes ELIXIR-DEV's change to tenant_template.ex only) or a CODE-DESIGNER decision about how provision_via_shared_connection/1's teardown should behave under on_exit -- both outside what §11.9.4 licenses ELIXIR-DEV to decide alone.

THE FIX APPLIED (test/support/tenant_template.ex, ensure_template!/0): the existing `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` statement (previously the function's unconditional first line) moved to become the first statement inside the existing `if template_ready?() do :ok else ... end` conditional's `else` branch, immediately before the existing `Repo.query!("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(...)")` call -- a pure reorder, zero new branches/functions/attributes. The function's own explanatory comment (previously lines 69-81) moved with it and was extended with one new paragraph stating the call is now conditional on template_ready?() == false and citing design §11.9.1-§11.9.2, per §11.9.4 item 1's explicit requirement not to move the call 'for no stated reason'. template_ready?/0, clone_tenant_schema!/1, assert_clone_parity!/3, build_template!/0, do_build_template!/1 and every other function in the file are byte-for-byte unchanged, matching §11.9.4 items 2-3. `@spec ensure_template!() :: :ok` unchanged.

`mix format --check-formatted`: clean, no output. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`: clean, 'Compiling 190 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings.

=== §11.7 REGRESSION PLAN, RUN IN FULL, REAL QUOTED OUTPUT ===

ITEM 1/ITEM 6 -- backfill_test.exs, the exact reproduction case (REQUIRED, permanent named regression check): `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs`, run repeatedly (fresh `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.reset` between some runs to rule out stale-state artefacts) -- every run returns `Result: 0/5 passed`, never the >=4/5 (target 5/5) §11.7 item 6 requires. Two consecutive same-DB runs showed DIFFERENT individual tests failing at different positions in the failure list (non-deterministic scheduling of which test hits which symptom first), but the aggregate is consistently 0/5. This IS an improvement in mechanism over the pre-§11.9 regression (§11.9's own diagnosed FK-does-not-exist symptom, `tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey does not exist`, no longer appears in isolated first-call-after-reset runs when the template is pre-built by an async:true caller in the SAME `mix test` invocation -- see below) -- but the file's aggregate result is still 0/5, not the required >=4/5, because of the second, unrelated defect described below.

CONTROL EXPERIMENT distinguishing §11.9's fix (which works) from the new defect (which does not fix): `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.reset` then `mix test test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs --trace --seed 0`. secrets_test.exs (async:true, template::clone default, routed via with_provisioning_repo/1 which never touches Letflow.Repo's mode) ran to completion first (`Result` line for it: 11 passed, 1 property, 10 tests -- confirmed in a separate solo run: `mix test test/letflow/secrets_test.exs` -> `Result: 11 passed (1 property, 10 tests)`), building the template. Then EVERY ONE of backfill_test.exs's 5 tests, per --trace, shows its own test BODY completing successfully (`(801.0ms)`/`(876.1ms)`/`(750.2ms)`/`(798.1ms)`/`(2370.9ms)` timing lines, i.e. the test's own assertions all passed) -- confirming §11.9's fix closed the original Mechanism-4/FK-does-not-exist hazard for the steady-state (template-already-built) case exactly as designed. But all 5 then fail during `on_exit` teardown:

```
1) test regression: ISS-0332 -- backfill updates pre-existing tenant to schema_version 2 (Letflow.TenantProvisioning.BackfillTest)
   ** (exit) exited in: DBConnection.Holder.checkout(#PID<0.860.0>, [log: ..., pool: DBConnection.Ownership, repo: Letflow.Repo, timeout: 15000, pool_size: 32])
       ** (EXIT) shutdown: "owner #PID<0.859.0> exited"
```
(identical shape, different PIDs, for all 5 tests; full stacktrace bottoms out at test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:740 Letflow.TenantFixture.schema_present?/1 -> :718 guarded/2 -> :549 log_teardown/3 -> :525 teardown/2 -> :370 provision_via_shared_connection/1 -> ExUnit.OnExitHandler.exec_callback/1).

ROOT CAUSE, traced to source, not guessed: ExUnit on_exit callbacks run in a process distinct from (and scheduled after) the test process itself has already terminated. test/support/data_case.ex sets `{:shared, self()}` sandbox mode for async:false tests (self() bound to the ORIGINAL test process). provision_via_shared_connection/1 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, added in commit c38dfa9b implementing design §11.2) deliberately issues NO Sandbox.mode/2 call and NO explicit checkout of its own -- it only reuses whatever connection is already ambient for the calling process (that is its entire, correctly-implemented, load-bearing property per §11.2 step 3). tenant_fixture.ex:303's on_exit registration -- `on_exit(fn -> connection_wrap.(fn -> teardown(tenant.id, owner) end) end)` -- closes over `connection_wrap = &provision_via_shared_connection/1` for this dispatch branch, so teardown's on_exit callback ALSO just reuses the ambient connection with no checkout of its own. By the time that on_exit callback actually runs, the original owner test process (self() from setup time) has already exited -- normal ExUnit lifecycle order -- and Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox's {:shared, owner_pid} mode ties the shared connection's lifetime to that owner process: once it is gone, ANY subsequent checkout attempt against Letflow.Repo (including one made on behalf of that same logical test, from its own on_exit callback process) raises exactly this `exit`/`shutdown: "owner ... exited"`. `guarded/2` (tenant_fixture.ex:717-721) and `log_teardown/3`'s own rescue clause (tenant_fixture.ex:556-558) both use `rescue`, which does NOT catch `exit` signals (only `raise`d exceptions) -- so neither of the two existing safety nets this code already has for exactly this kind of degraded-capture scenario actually catches this failure mode, and it propagates all the way up through the on_exit callback to ExUnit, which reports it as a failing test.

This is NOT scoped to backfill_test.exs. Independently reproduced on a second, unrelated async:false + template::clone caller: `mix test test/letflow/api/context_test.exs` -> `Result: 5/11 passed`, 6 failures, SAME shutdown/owner-exited shape (confirmed via grep on the failure output). This satisfies §11.7 item 2's requirement for a second, independently-verified instance of the same failure class -- except the class this run actually found is the teardown defect, not (only) the ISS-0332/Mechanism-4 class item 2 was written to corroborate.

BOUNDED, NOT SPECULATED: confirmed via `git stash` (isolating to the pre-§11.9, pre-this-handoff commit c38dfa9b) that BOTH failure counts are IDENTICAL on that commit: `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs` -> `Result: 0/5 passed`* and `mix test test/letflow/api/context_test.exs` -> `Result: 5/11 passed`, same shutdown/owner-exited symptom in both. (*Note: on c38dfa9b, backfill_test.exs's 0/5 is a mix of the ORIGINAL §11.9-diagnosed FK-does-not-exist symptom AND this teardown symptom, since §11.9's fix was not yet applied on that commit -- the teardown defect is confirmed independently via context_test.exs's identical 5/11 on both commits, and via the --trace evidence above showing backfill_test.exs's test BODIES passing post-§11.9-fix with only teardown failing.) This defect predates this handoff entirely -- it was introduced by commit c38dfa9b's own addition of provision_via_shared_connection/1 (design §11.2/§11.3), not by anything applied under this handoff's §11.9.4 authorization, and §10-only code (with_provisioning_repo/1's ProvisioningRepo path, which has its own separate :auto mode unaffected by Letflow.Repo's owner semantics) never exhibited it.

WHY THIS BLOCKS RATHER THAN BEING PATCHED AROUND: §11.9.4 authorizes ELIXIR-DEV to change exactly one file (test/support/tenant_template.ex) for exactly one reorder. Fixing the teardown defect requires changing test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's provision_via_shared_connection/1 and/or its on_exit teardown wiring (owned_modules for THIS run's design, per step-08's own context.owned_modules) -- a real mechanism decision (candidates this handoff does NOT choose among: have provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit teardown explicitly checkout/allow the connection for the on_exit process before running teardown/2; wrap log_teardown/3's guarded/2 to catch :exit as well as raised exceptions, matching INV-F-10's 'a failing log call must never turn a passing test red' intent, which this defect currently violates; or something else CODE-DESIGNER has not yet considered) that must go back through CODE-DESIGNER and be re-gated by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, per this project's design/implementation split and this handoff's own explicit instruction to stop rather than guess on something outside its authorized scope.

=== REMAINING §11.7 ITEMS, ALL CLEAN ===

ITEM 2 (second independent instance): test/letflow/api/context_test.exs run and confirmed exhibiting the SAME defect class (5/11 passed, identical shutdown/owner-exited shape) -- see above; also confirmed present identically pre-this-handoff.

ITEM 3 (tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs, :replay override branch): `mix test test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs` -> `Result: 2 passed`. Clean -- consistent with the diagnosis, since :replay always routes through with_provisioning_repo/1 (ProvisioningRepo), never provision_via_shared_connection/1, so it cannot hit this defect.

ITEM 4 (iss0480_provisioning_repo_isolation_test.exs, async:true regression): `mix test test/letflow/iss0480_provisioning_repo_isolation_test.exs` -> `Result: 1 passed`. Clean, unaffected, as expected (async:true path unchanged).

ITEM 5 (tenant_template_test.exs, NEW in this rework, must stay green unmodified): `mix test test/support/tenant_template_test.exs` -> `Result: 7 passed`. Clean -- confirms §11.9's reorder did not disturb ensure_template!/0's own observable contract, exactly as §11.7 item 5 anticipated.

=== WHAT WAS NOT DONE ===

Item 6's broader scoped run across TEST-RUNNER's originally-reported 18-19 failing files was not attempted at full scope: the teardown defect above is reproducible on at least 2 of those files already (backfill_test.exs, context_test.exs) and would contaminate a broader run's signal the same way step-08's handoff explicitly reasoned about for the ORIGINAL blocker -- a wider run right now would mix genuine §11.9-mechanism confirmation with this newly-found, unrelated defect and produce a noisy, unusable report rather than clean evidence either way.

No commit was made. The working tree contains: (1) test/support/tenant_template.ex's §11.9.4 reorder (compiles clean, formats clean, correctly closes the Mechanism-4/FK-does-not-exist hazard per the control experiment above), (2) lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md's rework-iteration-3 edits (already reviewed/approved by step-09b), (3) the two new handoff files from steps 09/09b. The tenant_template.ex fix should NOT be reverted -- it is independently verified correct and necessary -- but this run cannot proceed to SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER/the full-suite gate while backfill_test.exs's own named regression check (§11.7 item 6) still returns 0/5, for a reason outside this handoff's own scope to fix.

issues.description: provision_via_shared_connection/1 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, added by commit c38dfa9b implementing design §11.2/§11.3 -- predates and is independent of this handoff's §11.9.4 work) has a teardown defect: its on_exit callback (tenant_fixture.ex:303, `connection_wrap.(fn -> teardown(tenant.id, owner) end)`) reuses the ambient Letflow.Repo connection with no checkout/allow of its own, relying on {:shared, self()} mode set by test/support/data_case.ex at setup time. By the time ExUnit actually runs the on_exit callback, the original owner test process has already exited (normal ExUnit lifecycle order), so the shared connection is gone and the on_exit callback's own attempt to query it raises `** (exit) shutdown: "owner #PID exited"` from DBConnection.Holder.checkout/3 inside teardown/2 -> log_teardown/3 -> guarded/2 -> schema_present?/1. Neither guarded/2 (tenant_fixture.ex:717-721) nor log_teardown/3's own rescue (tenant_fixture.ex:556-558) catches this because both use `rescue`, which does not catch `exit` signals, only `raise`d exceptions -- so INV-F-10's 'a failing log call must never turn a passing test red' guarantee is currently violated for this specific failure shape. Reproduced on every async:false + template::clone TenantFixture caller tested: test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs (0/5, all 5 in teardown once §11.9's fix is applied and the template is pre-built) and test/letflow/api/context_test.exs (5/11, 6 failures, identical shape), both confirmed present identically on pre-this-handoff commit c38dfa9b via git stash, so this is NOT something introduced by §11.9.4's reorder. Fixing it requires changing test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (outside this handoff's owned_modules/authorization) or a new CODE-DESIGNER decision about how provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit teardown should acquire its connection -- must go back through CODE-DESIGNER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR before ELIXIR-DEV resumes, not be guessed at here.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER: diagnose and design a fix for provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit teardown defect (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, owned_modules for a new design pass) -- the shared-connection path's teardown must acquire a usable connection from within the on_exit callback's own process rather than assuming the original owner test process is still alive, and/or guarded/2 and log_teardown/3's failure boundaries must be widened to catch :exit as well as raised exceptions per INV-F-10's existing intent. test/support/tenant_template.ex's §11.9.4 fix (this handoff) is independently correct and should be preserved/committed once the new design is implemented and gated -- do not revert it while investigating the teardown defect.
